question.text: As per SEBI Circular dated January 12, 2024 on AIF custodian appointment, the custodian for a scheme of an AIF must be appointed:

answer.text: Prior to the date of first investment of the scheme.
Within 90 days of the first investment by the scheme.
Only before declaration of the final close of the fund.
Before the annual audit of the scheme's books of accounts.

explanation.text: **The Logic:** SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/AFD/PoD/CIR/2024/5 dated January 12, 2024 requires the custodian for a scheme of an AIF to be appointed PRIOR to the date of first investment of the scheme. This ensures that every security held by the AIF is safeguarded from day one. The custodian also must register under SEBI (Custodian) Regulations, 1996 and cannot be a related party to sponsor/designated partners unless specific conditions are met. **The Trap:** Option B invents a post-hoc window. Option C decouples custody from investment activity. Option D conflates custody with audit. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C tests identical timing. XIX-D tests same rule for Cat I/II. XXI-B tests PM-side custody. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Treat custodian onboarding as a first-drawdown gating item. The custodial agreement should cover: scope of demat accounts, physical-settlement workflow for commodity derivatives (Cat III specific), reporting cadence to SEBI, and reconciliation SLA. If the custodian is in the sponsor group, document the related-party test satisfying SEBI (AIF) 2024 amendment carve-out.
